global.headline: TRUMP RULES OUT STRIKING IRAN BEFORE THE MIDTERMS WHILE HOUTHI MISSILES CLOSE RIYADH'S AIRPORT A THIRD TIME
summary: Trump posted that the United States “will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd”, after reports he had spent days weighing new strikes. Diplomacy and economic pressure continue, he said, citing “productive discussions” with Tehran, and the naval blockade of Iranian ports “will remain in full force and effect”. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran would answer within days. A Reuters/Ipsos poll has 60 per cent of Americans, one in four Republicans among them, disapproving of his handling of the war, 26 days from the vote.

Explosions struck Riyadh for a third consecutive day, the Houthis claiming a ballistic missile on King Khalid International. Flightradar24 recorded the airport closed again, several airlines suspended Riyadh flights, a parked Saudia aircraft burned at a terminal, and interception debris hit a kindergarten and a medical complex. The coalition said it downed a missile north of Riyadh and destroyed the Sanaa launcher. Pakistan's military spokesman Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry confirmed Pakistani troops are already in the kingdom under the Mecca pact, numbers classified. UKMTO said the tanker Acers was hit by projectiles 94km off Qatar's north coast, casualties unquantified; the IMO counts at least 24 seafarers killed in 93 incidents since the war began. A Congressional Research Service update puts US aircraft lost or damaged at 81, up from 42 in May — half MQ-9 Reapers, plus an F-35A and an E-3 Sentry — costed by the CBO at US$1.9–3.3b.
global.geopolitical: A pause measured against an American election tells Tehran how long it has and the Gulf states absorbing the missiles that the clock is domestic — which is why Riyadh, not Washington, is invoking a treaty and importing Pakistani troops.
global.socioeconomic: Markets read it as thin: Brent jumped over 5 per cent on the strike reports, touched almost US$106 and still closed up 4 per cent at US$104.28, WTI up 3.6 per cent at US$91.49 — the blockade he promised to keep being the part that removes barrels.

global.headline: A RUSSIAN GLIDE BOMB BURNS TWO CITY BUSES IN KRAMATORSK, KILLING AT LEAST 33
summary: Police said a glide bomb hit a Kramatorsk street where two city buses were operating, killing at least 33 and wounding 18 by the national police count, 22 by the Donetsk governor's. Zelensky said the toll could rise, that two of the dead were not yet identified, and that the attack “will not go unanswered”. All public transport in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk was suspended. It is the year's deadliest single strike, above the 33 killed across Kyiv in a July barrage, and came a day after the Pryluky block strike.
global.geopolitical: Glide bombs are released from aircraft inside Russian airspace, so Kyiv's only answer is the deep strike it has been denied the range for — making each attack an argument aimed at Washington.
global.socioeconomic: Shutting the buses in two cities of the Donetsk agglomeration removes the only way out for residents without cars, who are most of those still there.

global.headline: ETHIOPIAN DRONES HIT ERITREAN TROOPS INSIDE TIGRAY DAYS AFTER THE TWO STATES CUT TIES
summary: The conflict monitor ACLED said “Eritrean troops and ammunition” in the Adigrat area of northern Tigray were hit by multiple drone strikes overnight Wednesday into Thursday. Witnesses described a massive night explosion, destroyed Eritrean lorries and troops withdrawing northward; Asmara's forces reportedly crossed the border this week and took positions around Adigrat. Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of arming Tigrayan rebels and the two severed relations last week; Eritrea's information minister accused Ethiopia of constructing “a fallacious narrative of ‘self-defence’”, without addressing the movements. Neither government has confirmed the strikes; the reporting rests on a single AFP account and anonymous witnesses.
global.geopolitical: The first reported Ethiopian fire on Eritrean forces since the 2018 peace that won Abiy Ahmed a Nobel turns a war over Tigray's factions into a war between two states, with that peace's co-signatory now a combatant.
global.socioeconomic: Adigrat sits on the highway from the Eritrean border down to Mekelle, the road relief convoys use, so fighting there puts resupply of a region still short of food behind a front line rather than a checkpoint.

global.headline: MATHEMATICIANS MOVE TO BOYCOTT OPENAI AFTER 722 MACHINE-WRITTEN PROOFS LAND ON GITHUB
summary: OpenAI published 722 manuscripts in 372 result families to a public GitHub repository on 6 October, produced by an unreleased internal frontier model from roughly 4,000 posed open problems. The headline claim is a quasi-Riemann hypothesis — Dirichlet L-functions, zeta included, having no zeros above a fixed real part, reported variously as 7/8 and 11/12 — not the Riemann hypothesis, which needs 1/2, but the first time anyone has cleared a fixed strip; others cover the Unique Games Conjecture and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. Lean formalisations accompany 235 families, none are peer reviewed, and Sam Altman framed the results as unconfirmed.

The Association for Human Mathematics called on mathematicians to stop working with OpenAI, a statement Terence Tao republished on his blog on 7 October. The repository's change log that day records three manuscripts withdrawn after a sign error undermined an argument and the work depending on it, and Steven Miller has accused OpenAI of reusing his 2016 sphere-packing argument without credit. OpenAI says it consulted the Institute for Advanced Study's advisory group on mathematics and AI; analyses say its recommendations were only partly adopted.
global.geopolitical: Authority over what counts as proven has moved, provisionally, from journals to a company's repository and its changelog — a precedent any lab can copy in any field where the referees are unpaid and the claims too numerous to check.
global.socioeconomic: Verification, not generation, is now the scarce input: Lean confirms that a proof's logic closes, not that the problem was worth posing or correctly framed, so the cost of 722 manuscripts falls on the people least able to bill for it.

global.headline: ITALY'S PARLIAMENT HANDS THE ELECTION WINNER 105 BONUS SEATS, ON A SECRET BALLOT
summary: The lower house approved Giorgia Meloni's electoral overhaul 227 to 164 in a secret ballot, the last of four votes. Seats go proportionally, and the party or coalition with the largest share takes 105 extra — 70 in the Chamber, 35 in the Senate — if it clears 42 per cent in both, raised from 40 in earlier drafts. Meloni wrote that “whoever wins must be able to govern”; Elly Schlein said the Democratic Party would win under any system, and Italia Viva's Maria Elena Boschi called it power preservation after the government lost its justice-reform referendum. It also lets voters choose among candidates on party lists, weakening leaders' control over who is elected. It goes to President Sergio Mattarella and may face the Constitutional Court; the election is due next year.
global.geopolitical: A G7 democracy has rewritten its seat allocation a year before voting, by secret ballot — and polling has Meloni's coalition behind, so the bonus she legislated is as likely to be collected by the centre-left.
global.socioeconomic: The 42 per cent double threshold is the whole mechanism: clear it and Italy gets the durable majority its borrowing costs have never been priced for, miss it and the law returns the same fragmented chamber with a fresh reason to litigate.

singapore.headline: INDONESIA'S PRESIDENT IS SUED OVER THE HAZE AS JOHOR SHUTS EVERY SCHOOL FOR TWO DAYS
summary: Four plaintiffs, among them the local chapter of the Indigenous organisation AMAN, sued President Prabowo Subianto and nine others in a Pontianak court over “gross negligence” on the recurring fires, seeking healthcare costs and a national-disaster declaration to unlock recovery funds. None of the ten appeared at the first hearing on 7 October, adjourned to 21 October; their lawyer Glorio Sanen suggested the smog itself might explain the absence. Johor closed all state schools for two days from 8 October on the Regent's directive, asking employers to give working parents flexibility. In Singapore the 24-hour PSI stayed unhealthy overnight and 1-hour PM2.5 was elevated in all five regions at 6.44am Friday; NEA says conditions may ease during the day.
singapore.geopolitical: Liability for the haze is being tested in an Indonesian court rather than through the ASEAN transboundary haze agreement — the one forum Singapore and Malaysia can invoke, and the one that has never produced a remedy.
singapore.socioeconomic: The cost stays distributed and unpriced: Johor absorbs two days of closed schools, Singapore a fourth day of unhealthy air, and neither can recover anything from whoever lit the fires.

singapore.headline: LTA PROPOSES MERGING COE CATEGORIES A AND B INTO ONE CAR CLASS, WITH REBATES SET BY CAR VALUE
summary: LTA opened a public consultation proposing to merge Categories A and B into one passenger-car category bidding from a single pool, with a feebate keyed to open market value: lower-value cars receive rebates, mid-range cars are unadjusted, higher-value cars pay a surcharge, keeping premium buyers above mass-market buyers. Bands would be drawn from the percentile distribution of median OMVs and reviewed annually, with three-band and five-band options — the five-band version adding S$7,500 steps either way for finer adjustment — and LTA is asking how Category E should work if A and B merge. Its stated reason is that manufacturers now specify higher-end models down to fit Category A's engine-power ceiling. The consultation closes on 2 November, findings early next year; analysts said the changes may stabilise premiums but are unlikely to lower them. Cat A closed the first October round at S$130,001.
singapore.geopolitical: Car ownership is the most visible rationing the state runs, and reopening its architecture mid-term invites the complaint that the categories were gamed for years before LTA moved — which is what the consultation is designed to absorb.
singapore.socioeconomic: One pool ends the arbitrage that let a detuned luxury car bid against a family hatchback, but it also puts them in the same auction: the feebate does all the separating, and S$7,500 a band is small against a S$130,001 premium.

singapore.headline: A FULL-TIME NATIONAL SERVICEMAN DIES AFTER A FALL AT BASIC MILITARY TRAINING SCHOOL 3 ON PULAU TEKONG
summary: MINDEF said a full-time national serviceman was found unconscious at about 1.22pm at the foot of a building at Basic Military Training School 3, was treated at the Pulau Tekong Medical Centre, evacuated by helicopter to Singapore General Hospital arriving at 2.05pm, and pronounced dead at 2.27pm. It said he was not involved in training at the time. Police said they were alerted to a fall from height, found the man motionless at the foot of the building, and that investigations continue. Mothership reported his age as 20; MINDEF's statement did not give it, and no cause of death has been stated.
singapore.geopolitical: Conscription here rests on the expectation that a son sent to Tekong comes back, so the account of each such death is a question of the institution's standing — and MINDEF's early emphasis that no training was involved is where that scrutiny starts.
singapore.socioeconomic: It lands inside a safety episode already running: MOM's voluntary time-out for construction and transport firms covers 5 to 18 October, after seven workplace deaths since September.

singapore.headline: WONG TELLS GLOBAL CHIEF EXECUTIVES THE AI RALLY WILL CORRECT AND SINGAPORE SHOULD SPEND THE WINDOW
summary: At the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore, PM Lawrence Wong said the AI-driven tech rally has been good for growth but that bubbles have an expiration date and a correction will come, and that the task is to use the window to build capability, attract investment and create better jobs before momentum fades. Demand for AI chips has spilled into logistics and professional services, he said, pressing the tripartite arrangement so gains are distributed rather than pooling at the top, and restating that the priority is protecting workers rather than every individual job.
singapore.geopolitical: Saying the correction out loud to the people choosing where the next data centre goes is positioning: Singapore as the jurisdiction that keeps the investment through the downturn, two days after Parliament licensed two-thirds of its data centres.
singapore.socioeconomic: H1 growth of 6.1 per cent leaned on exactly the semiconductor and AI-linked demand he is warning about, and “protecting workers, not jobs” is the admission that the adjustment will be visible in individual employment.

singapore.headline: CRYSTAL JADE SHUTS FOUR MORE OUTLETS AND ENDS ABOUT 120 JOBS AS RECEIVERS PREPARE A SALE
summary: Kroll, receiver since 29 September over the holding companies of the Singapore and Hong Kong operations, said on 7 October that the Singapore restructuring was done. Four outlets stopped trading on 6 October — La Mian Xiao Long Bao at Bugis Junction, Toa Payoh and i12 Katong, and Crystal Jade GO at Oasis Terraces in Punggol — and about 120 staff across those outlets and selected corporate functions received termination notices, leaving roughly 210 employees and nine operating outlets. Kroll expects no further Singapore closures and will market the group as a going concern to preserve the brands; the central kitchen, Crystal Jade Food Manufacturing, sits outside the receivership and closed on 5 October. Kroll has engaged the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union since 30 September; the union and e2i have identified more than 400 openings in food services, hospitality and retail.
singapore.geopolitical: The Singapore and Hong Kong holdings sit in one receivership, so the sale prices one of the more widely franchised Singaporean consumer brands at the moment a buyer can see how thin the mid-market dining model had become.
singapore.socioeconomic: About a third of the Singapore workforce has gone in a week, and the 400 openings are the test rather than the answer: whether displaced restaurant staff re-place at comparable pay decides if this reads as one brand failing or a sector repricing.

word.definition: Deliberate restraint from exercising a power or right one holds — in law, a creditor's choice not to enforce a debt yet, without surrendering the claim.
word.etymology: From Old English forberan, “to bear with, endure, abstain”, from for- “away, off” and beran “to carry”. The narrower legal sense of withholding enforcement of a right while keeping it settled in sixteenth-century English law, and survives in mortgage and loan practice.
word.example: Trump's undertaking not to attack Iran before 3 November is forbearance rather than peace: the blockade stays “in full force and effect”, nothing has been conceded, and what Tehran has been handed is the date on which the right to strike resumes.
